F_m(r)=p(1-r^m)/(1+r^m)-2r^N/(1-r) is strictly decreasing for 0<r<1, p in (0,2], N,m>=1; F_m(0+)=p and F_m(1-)=-infinity ensure unique sharp root. Increasing m increases F_m at each interior r, so R_{m+1}>R_m; evaluating F_m(A)=-2p A^m/(1+A^m)<0 at unique A solving p=2A^N/(1-A) bounds R_m<A<1. Monotone limit L satisfies L=A because R_m^m<=A^m->0. Mean value theorem between R_m and A and bound m*xi_m^(m-1)<=m*A^(m-1)->0 give the exact asymptotic deficit (A-R_m)/A^m -> 2A(1-A)/[N-(N-1)A]. Substitution N=1 recovers 4p/(p+2)^2. Independently bisection checked p=1,2 N=1 and p=1.2 N=3 at m=15,40; normalized ratios approach 1. Assumption that the root is the sharp radius is imported from cited prior theorem, not proven by this audit.
